title: Graduated traffic curves and stability‑led rollback gates
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a graduated rollout system that uses configurable traffic curves (time-based percentage ramps), stability‑led gates (based on error and SLI windows), and automated rollback triggers tied to our feature‑flag system and versioning channels (stable / LTS / experimental). This ticket covers design, implementation, e2e tests, dashboards, and a small pilot on internal non-customer clusters.

Goals: 1) Provide traffic curve primitives (linear, exponential, custom) that operators can attach to releases; 2) Define stability‑led gates computed from short and medium SLI windows with hysteresis to avoid flapping; 3) Wire rollout controller to feature flags and model version pins so we can rollback or fast‑forward automatically; 4) Ensure the system respects LTS and stable channel semantics (no auto-escalation into LTS without explicit opt-in); 5) Deliver production dashboards and alert rules for rollout health.

Out of scope (for this ticket): manual safe rollback UI polish, full multi-region routing fusion, and enterprise RBAC policy editing UI.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic curves available as reusable objects in rollout manifests and can be applied to a release
Controller evaluates stability gates every 30s and pauses/rolls back when thresholds breached
Rollouts integrate with feature flags so percentage routing uses the same flag state as application clients
Automated rollback emits audit event and a GitHub PR to revert release plan or pin prior model version
Dashboards show rollout progress, 1/5/50/95 latency percentiles, error rate, and inflight token counts
Runbook updated and at least one dry run completed on internal cluster with simulated faults
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: RFC draft posted to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood/company/release/grad-rollouts) — initial design and examples for curves
2026-01-25: Design review with Platform and Observability — agreed on 2 SLI windows (60s, 10m) and hysteresis delta of 25%
2026-02-02: PoC controller built that can apply linear and sigmoid curves to traffic allocations; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8157
2026-02-18: Integration spike with feature-flag service completed; added SDK hooks for percent-based routing logic
2026-02-28: Canary pilot on internal-test region: applied exponential curve to runtime-1.22 canary; observed graceful ramp and one gateway timeout incident at 35% traffic
2026-03-05: Added stability gate evaluation and auto-rollback policy (error-rate > 1.5% sustained for 2m triggers rollback); automated rollback executed successfully during simulated fault
2026-03-10: Observability dashboards linked and alert rules tuned. Began documentation handoff to SRE runbook owners
implementation_notes:
Controller: new rollout-controller service (go) that subscribes to release events, computes target allocations per traffic curve, and emits routing updates to the traffic-router. Feature flags: use percentage bucketing from flags service to ensure deterministic routing for clients that use SDKs. Auto-rollback: two-tier action — (1) soft pause (zero rate increase) with on-call notify, (2) hard rollback after configurable confirmation window. Rollout manifests stored in Git with release metadata and channel labels.

Data & thresholds: rely on existing ingest of per-route SLIs from metrics pipeline; evaluation uses two windows (short: 60s, medium: 10m) and weighted scoring. Scoring formula = max(short_err_score * 1.2, medium_err_score). Hysteresis: require breach to persist for 75% of evaluation window.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use deterministic feature-flag bucketing to avoid client-server divergence rather than pure router sampling
Tradeoff: Tight short windows give fast detection at cost of false positives — mitigated with hysteresis and medium window confirmation
Decision: Do not auto-promote to LTS/stable channel — promotions must be explicit and gated by QA + manual signoff
Tradeoff: Controller complexity vs. safety — opted for simple, auditable steps (pause -> notify -> rollback) rather than opaque ML-based decisions
test_plan: Unit tests for curve math and allocation invariants
Integration tests: controller + router + flags in local k8s cluster using traffic-replay harness
Chaos test: inject 5s tail latency on canary instances and verify rollback triggers
E2E pilot: staged rollout to internal-test region with canary -> gradual ramp -> rollback scenario
Post-merge: dark traffic experiments in prod for 48h before opening real traffic ramps
risks: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks; misaligned bucketing between SDK and router; alert fatigue from too-sensitive thresholds. Mitigations: conservative defaults, pilot and dark traffic, runbook and on-call playbook.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: please focus on the stability scoring formula and the default hysteresis values. Pay attention to the feature-flag bucketing compatibility section in the PR. Expect a follow-up ticket to add multi-region reconciliation and RBAC controls.
final_notes: Next steps: finish RFC feedback loop, merge controller PR, run dark traffic experiments, and schedule 2-week pilot. If pilot is stable, follow-up ticket will add canary-to-LTS promotion workflow with manual approvals.
